jobs.description: Technical University Munich operates the high flux Neutron Source Heinz Maier-Leibnitz (FRM II) located at the scientific campus in Garching, Germany. The neutron source itself, its research instruments as well as the irradiation facilities provide unique possibilities for the scientific and industrial use of neutron beams.In the group Neutron Imaging, we are offering a full-time scientist position (40 hours / week) asInstrument Scientist Neutron Imaging (m/f/d)The Neutron Imaging Group at the FRM II operates two world-leading instruments, ANTARES and NECTAR, providing complementary capabilities for radiography and tomography with neutrons. The group plays a key role in advancing methodological development in neutron imaging worldwide.ANTARES is a versatile imaging instrument using thermal and cold neutrons for a broad range of radiography and tomography applications. NECTAR can switch between thermal- and fast-neutron operation and offers worldwide unique capabilities for fast-neutron imaging, enabling the investigation of large and highly absorbing samples that are difficult to access with conventional neutron or X-ray imaging. In recent years, multimodal imaging approaches combining neutron imaging with complementary imaging and characterization techniques have gained increasing importance for the quantitative characterization of materials and functional systems. The complementary capabilities of ANTARES and NECTAR provide an excellent basis for developing and applying such approaches.You will work across our neutron imaging activities at ANTARES and NECTAR, with a particular focus on fast-neutron imaging and the operation and further development of NECTAR. Plant organs (leaves, stems and roots) and soil samples will beanalysed for metal concentrations.- Contributing to data collection, formatting and management, and maintainingdetailed records of protocols and procedures.- Following appropriate hygiene and safety procedures when handling plant andsoil samples with elevated metal concentrations, both in the field and in thelaboratory.You have the following skills and knowledge:- A Bachelor’s degree in ecology or an equivalent qualification.- English proficiency at B2 level or above; C1 or C2 preferred forcommunication with international partners.- Basic knowledge of functional ecology and methods for measuringabove-ground and root functional traits.- An understanding of major plant adaptations to exposure to metals andmetalloids.- Experience in sample collection and international transport, includingrelevant regulatory requirements.- Experience in functional trait measurements using specialist software suchas WinFolia and WinRhizo.- Enjoyment of fieldwork and the physical fitness required for potentiallydemanding conditions, including mountainous terrain and remote areas.- Precision and thoroughness in laboratory work, which will account for asubstantial proportion of the role, particularly when handling plant and soilsamples with elevated metal concentrations.- Clear and open communication with a range of stakeholders, includinginternational researchers.- The ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously, meet deadlines andadapt to changing workloads.- A valid Category B driving licence.- Willingness and ability to travel to the United States for fieldwork,subject to applicable travel and entry requirements; travel expenses will becovered by the project.Here are the benefits we offer:- The opportunity to develop your career at an internationally renownedresearch museum.- A friendly, dynamic and interdisciplinary working environment.- An attractive workplace in central Stuttgart.- A subsidised public transport ticket (JobTicket BW).- Generous core hours, flexible working arrangements and the option to workremotely.- Core funding for research and conference travel.- The opportunity to participate in established research projects at theState Museum of Natural History Stuttgart (SMNS).- Family-friendly working conditions.- Support with learning German, if required.Please submit your application exclusively via our website, including:- A cover letter outlining your motivation and a CV.- The names and contact details of two referees.- Copies of relevant certificates.Applications are welcome in English. We strongly encourage women to apply.Diversity and inclusion are central to our values: applications from peoplewith severe disabilities will be given priority where candidates are equallyqualified.
